newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes firm as stocks rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes firm as stocks rally.

text.p: The Mexican peso held on to early strength to close slightly firmer on Wednesday as local and foreign dealers sold dollars to invest in the stock market, traders said.

Traders said that the inflow of dollars shored the peso up against weakness that may otherwise have arisen from Tuesday night's fall in primary Cetes rates. The bellwether 28-day Cetes rate fell to 23.06 percent, down 22 basis points from last week.

"The market is still liquid, the Cetes results had little impact...I think the peso did not firm up any more because conditions apparently lend themselves to some options being exercised," said a trader, referring to dollar puts sold by Banco de Mexico.
The benchmark 48-hour and 24 hour contracts closed 0.15 and 0.2 of a centavo firmer, respectively, at 7.5170/7.5210 and 7.5130/7.5170.
The same-day peso had closed earlier 1.2 centavos firmer at 7.5095/7.5130 per dollar.
Trade was thin, but demand for dollars was very light, so demand for pesos prevailed.

"The inflow of dollars has not been spectacular, but it has at least been steady, and that can be seen in the bolsa," a trader said. "There have been enough dollars in supply to keep the peso stable."
The Bolsa's leading IPC index was up 49.22 points, or 1.50 percent, at 3,335.70 when the peso market closed.
"The peso is still strong despite the primary auction and negative comments by a certain well-known person," said a trader, referring to U.S. economict Rudiger Dornbusch.
Dornbusch had been quoted by Mexican daily newspaper Reforma on Tuesday as saying that Banco de Mexico was pegging the peso and this was a risky policy.
"There is no reason why the peso should not stay where it is over the coming days if currently favorable circumstances continue," a trader said.
